eligibility.out_of_class_discretionary.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(f) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
eligibility.out_of_class_discretionary.summary: A public officer has discretion to respond to public records requests made by nonresidents; responding to one nonresident request does not waive the officer's right to deny other or future nonresident requests.

eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-40(a) (amended by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.summary: The right to inspect and copy is granted to every resident without any condition that the requester state or justify a purpose; no statement of purpose is required to make a request.

custody.custodian_definition_and_role.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
custody.custodian_definition_and_role.summary: 'Public officer' means a public officer or his or her designee responsible for responding to public records requests; this identifies who must respond and to whom requests route.

custody.request_tracking.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(5) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
custody.request_tracking.summary: At or around the time of designating a request as time-intensive, the public officer shall record it in a log of currently pending time-intensive requests identifying the requester's name and the date of acknowledgment; the log is confidential and not subject to disclosure under this article (tho…

intake.procedures_publication.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-45(a)(1) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
intake.procedures_publication.summary: A resident may request access to a public record by following the written procedures established by the public officer having custody; those procedures may set a standard form, a designated recipient (e.g., a public records coordinator), permissible transmission methods, and other submission poli…

intake.procedures_publication.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-45(a)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
intake.procedures_publication.summary: The public officer shall make its written procedures concerning public records reasonably available to the public.

fee.schedule_and_authority.summary: A public officer may require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before the requester may receive any public records (standard request); more generally, a certified copy is furnished on payment of a reasonable fee.

classification.processing_track.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
classification.processing_track.summary: A 'standard request' is one that seeks specifically and discretely identified records the public officer determines would take less than eight hours of staff time to process (identifying, retrieving, and redacting/withholding protected information), requiring no or minimal clarification; it route…

classification.processing_track.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-43(b)(6) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
classification.processing_track.summary: A 'time-intensive request' is one the public officer determines would take more than eight hours of staff time to process (identifying, retrieving, and redacting/withholding protected information); it routes to the time-intensive track.

classification.processing_track.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
classification.processing_track.summary: The public officer shall notify the requester within 15 business days after acknowledging receipt that the request qualifies as a time-intensive request, and shall at that time notify the requester of any likely fees.

classification.processing_track.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
classification.processing_track.summary: Upon the time-intensive designation notice, the officer shall allow the requester to withdraw the time-intensive request and submit a new request that is not time-intensive; the requester may instead elect to proceed.

payment.advance_payment.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(2) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
payment.advance_payment.summary: For a time-intensive request, the public officer shall require the requester to pay a reasonable fee set by the public officer before providing a substantive response.

response.classified_request_window.authority: Ala. Code § 36-12-44(b)(4) (added by SB270, 2024 Reg. Sess.)
response.classified_request_window.summary: If the requester elects to proceed with a time-intensive request, the public officer shall provide a substantive response fulfilling or denying the request within 45 business days after the requester elected to proceed.
response.classified_request_window.clock_spec: 45 business-days from the requester's election to proceed
